chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:
If a boy steals and has not reached puberty, his fingertips are cut.

And Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "A غلام was brought to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام who had stolen and had not reached puberty, so he cut from the flesh of the ends of his fingers. Then he said: If you return, I will cut your hand."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَا: Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.إِنْ عُدْتَ: if you return; if you repeat the offense
key_terms.اَلصَّبِيُّ: a minor boy who has not yet reached legal maturity
key_terms.اَلْحُلُمَ: puberty; the threshold of legal responsibility
key_terms.قُطِعَتْ أَنَامِلُهُ: his fingertips were cut; a reduced corporal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith if a child who has not reached puberty commits theft?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning theft committed by a minor who has not yet reached puberty. It reports that a lesser corporal punishment was applied before full legal liability, along with a warning of the fixed punishment upon repetition.
